notes: Candidates from feedback themes (ingest). Not counted as an inspector in detection k of N. Each must be reproduced by the finding verifier before it becomes a finding.

candidates.title: Change dates is only reachable through an unlabelled three-dot menu on the berth list
candidates.description: On the choose-berth page the stay summary ("Arriving on … at …, staying …") is plain text and there is no visible date control or "Change" link. The only route to change dates is the icon-only "More options" button (three dots), whose menu contains "Change dates". Skippers who want to move their arrival by a day do not associate a three-dot icon with dates.
candidates.impact: Skippers abandon the berth list, restart the booking or phone the office to change a date — a core task in PRODUCT.md.
candidates.recommendation: Put a visible "Change dates" link next to the stay summary on the berth list; keep the menu item if wanted.

evidence.detail: theme TH-01-date-change-hidden; prevalence pooled 15/100 people; by channel tickets 3/36, survey 4/34, reviews 2/24, usability 6/6

factor_notes.frequency: tickets: 3 of 36 people; survey: 4 of 34 people; reviews: 2 of 24 people; usability: 6 of 6 people (self-selected channels count reporters, not users)

candidates.title: The "Booking stopped / BK-409" state gives no reason, no next step and no way back

criteria.name: Every stop in the booking says what to do next

candidates.description: When the entered length exceeds the chosen berth's limit, the boat form is hidden and replaced by "Booking stopped" and "This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409." There is no explanation that the boat is too long for the berth, no suggestion of a berth that fits, no link back to the berth list, and the typed details are not kept.
candidates.impact: Skippers cannot recover inside the booking; they close the browser, restart and retype, or phone the office.
candidates.recommendation: Say in plain words that the boat (length X m) is longer than the berth limit (Y m), offer the berths that fit with a link back to the list, and keep the typed boat details.

candidates.title: Tide table is in UTC while arrival times are local, with no conversion or warning
candidates.description: The tide table caption reads "High water at the quay, times in UTC" while the arrival-time select and the rest of the booking use local clock time (BST in October until the 25th). Nothing converts the times or warns that they differ by an hour, so skippers matching their arrival to high water read the table as local time.
candidates.impact: Skippers arrive an hour off the sill-gate window and wait outside or miss the gate — a safety-relevant fact per PRODUCT.md.
candidates.recommendation: Show tide times in local time (BST/GMT as applicable) and label the zone; keep UTC only as a secondary column if passage planners want it.

candidates.title: Arrival-time list offers and accepts times when the sill gate is closed, with no warning

criteria.name: Show the tide window wherever a time is chosen

candidates.description: The arrival-time select lists every hour from 06:00 to 21:00 regardless of the chosen date. The gate is open only about two hours either side of high water, but choosing e.g. 10:00 on 17 October (HW 14:32 UTC) and pressing "Check berths" proceeds with no warning and no display of the gate window next to the field.
candidates.impact: Skippers book an arrival they cannot make and only find out at the harbour entrance.
candidates.recommendation: Show the gate window for the chosen date next to the time field and either limit the list to times inside it or warn before continuing.

candidates.title: Boat "Length" field does not say length overall (LOA)
candidates.description: The boat page field is labelled only "Length" with no hint, while berth limits are length overall including bowsprit. Skippers with a bowsprit enter hull length and pass the check for a berth they do not fit.
candidates.impact: A boat can be booked into a berth it is too long for; the office has to correct it on arrival.
candidates.recommendation: Label it "Length overall (LOA) in metres" with a hint "including bowsprit and davits".

candidates.title: Boat "Length" field states no unit, unlike "Draught in metres"
candidates.description: The Length label gives no unit; the neighbouring Draught field says "in metres". Any positive number is accepted, so a length in feet (e.g. 34) passes validation and then ends at the unexplained BK-409 stop because it exceeds every berth limit.
candidates.impact: Skippers who think in feet enter feet and hit a dead end, or have to guess the unit.
candidates.recommendation: Put "in metres" in the label and flag implausible values (for example over 15) with "Enter the length in metres".

candidates.title: MMSI is required and unexplained, blocking boats without a DSC radio
candidates.description: The MMSI field has no hint explaining what it is, and leaving it blank shows "Enter the MMSI" and stops the booking. Small day sailers and some charter boats have no MMSI. PRODUCT.md says the booking needs only what the office needs to reach the skipper (name and mobile).
candidates.impact: Skippers without an MMSI cannot complete the booking online; others stall at the field.
candidates.recommendation: Explain MMSI in a hint and make it optional ("if your boat has a DSC radio").

candidates.title: Boat form is emptied whenever the page is shown, including after Back

criteria.name: Never lose what a skipper has typed

candidates.description: A pageshow handler resets the boat form every time the page is shown, so returning with the browser Back button (from review, or after the stop state) leaves Boat name, Length, Draught and MMSI empty.
candidates.impact: Skippers retype every field on a phone, often at sea, or give up.
candidates.recommendation: Remove the reset and repopulate the fields from the address parameters (they already carry boat, loa, draught and mmsi).

candidates.title: Confirmation page gives no arrival instructions (VHF channel, gate time for the day)
candidates.description: After booking, confirmed.html shows the booking but no VHF channel to call on approach and no gate opening times for the arrival day. Verifier should confirm the absence from the rendered text of the page.
candidates.impact: Skippers phone the office or wait outside the harbour for the gate.
candidates.recommendation: Add an "On arrival" block: the VHF channel, the gate window for the arrival date in local time, and the office number.

candidates.title: Berth list shows only per-metre-per-night rates; the stay total first appears on review
candidates.description: Each berth option shows "£x per metre per night" only. The total for the stay is shown first on the review page. The boat length is not yet known on the berth list, so a total there needs either the length earlier or an example total.
candidates.impact: Skippers compare berths by doing mental or calculator arithmetic.
candidates.recommendation: Ask for length overall before the berth list (it also lets the list hide berths that do not fit) and show the stay total per berth.

candidates.title: The booked thing is called "visitor berth", "pontoon space" and "mooring" on different pages
candidates.description: Headings change vocabulary across the journey: "Book a visitor berth" (/), "Choose a pontoon space" (berths), "Check your mooring booking" (review). Skippers wonder whether these are different products or prices.
candidates.impact: Doubt about whether the right thing was booked; extra checking.
candidates.recommendation: Use "berth" throughout, the word in PRODUCT.md and in the skippers' own words.

candidates.title: Booking pages show no step count or progress
candidates.description: None of the four booking pages (plan, berth, boat, review) shows "Step n of 4" or similar. Verifier should confirm the absence on each.
candidates.impact: Skippers on poor signal cannot judge whether they will finish before losing coverage.
candidates.recommendation: Add "Step n of 4" above each h1.

candidates.title: Booking pages reported slow or timing out on weak mobile data
candidates.description: Three reporters say the booking site was slow or timed out on 4G at sea (one had no signal at all). Verifier should check page weight, request count and render-blocking resources under a throttled network; field conditions cannot be reproduced locally.
candidates.recommendation: Only if measurement shows weight or blocking resources: inline critical CSS and keep pages small.
